supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:58 UTC, WS-ICHEN-01 had a connection to the explicit proxy on port 8080 with 50,000,389 originator bytes and 9,017 responder bytes. This establishes a large transfer to the proxy, but not its ultimate destination or whether it completed an upload to an external service.

After the large transfer, Ivy Chen's Chrome browser accessed aws.amazon.com and AWS static resources, including an AWS console page, through the proxy. These later requests do not establish that the earlier large transfer was to AWS or related to this browsing.

At 14:13:46 UTC, Sysmon recorded svchost.exe accessing LSASS with GrantedAccess=0x1010. A later record shows services.exe accessing LSASS with GrantedAccess=0x1000. The records establish process-access events, but do not establish that either was malicious or connected to the large transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: Per the supplied sensor coverage status, WS-ICHEN-01 winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the large-transfer event; therefore process attribution and relevant host activity in that interval are unavailable.

Per the supplied sensor coverage status, proxy collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the large-transfer event; the destination URL, proxy user, user agent, and external service for that transfer are not present in the available records.
Zeek connection and DNS collection was reported available, but the supplied record for the large transfer identifies only the internal proxy as the connection destination.
claims_not_established: What external destination, URL, or service received the bytes sent to the proxy at 13:45:58 UTC.
Which process or user action generated the large transfer, and whether it was an intentional upload, an approved activity, or data exfiltration.
Whether the later AWS console browsing was related to the earlier transfer or involved any data upload.
Whether the LSASS process-access event was legitimate or malicious, and whether it was related to the transfer.
Whether the scheduled svc-render password rotation and manual job update occurred as planned or were related to activity on WS-ICHEN-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including request URLs, authenticated user, user agent, byte counts, and any TLS inspection details for the connection associated with the 13:45:58 flow.
Obtain endpoint process and network telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01 covering 13:30–14:10 UTC, including process creation, file access, and network-to-process attribution.
Review endpoint evidence for the 14:13:46 LSASS access, including the svchost service and process command line, and determine whether memory was read or dumped.
Review FILE-NWD-01 and change records for the svc-render password rotation and manual RenderQueue update, including the responsible account and any resulting file or network activity.
Determine whether AWS access and any AWS uploads from Ivy Chen's account or WS-ICHEN-01 were authorized.
